sentences.text: ?Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 7885 of 2022

Applicant :- Man Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Anupam Laloriya
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.

Heard Sri Atif Ahmad, Advocate holding brief of Sri Anupam Laloriya, learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the papers on record.
2. The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no. 317 of 2020,
u/s 420, 504, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Mandi Dhanaura, District Amroha.

3. As per prosecution case, the instant applicant wrested Rs.12 Lakh from the husband of the first informant on the pretext of procuring him a job in Income Tax Department, but neither the job was procured nor he returned the money.

It is alleged in the F.I.R. that the creditor (husband of the first informant) died in an accident in 2019, thereafter, the first informant kept on demanding her money back but the applicant not only avoided the payment but also threatened her of her life.
Due to intervention of certain persons, he offered to pay Rs.6,86,000/- and executed a compromise deed.
However, he did not comply and the debtors cheque of Rs.1 Lakh for payment also bounced.
4. It is contended on behalf of the applicant that he is innocent.
He was ready to pay the amount but could not pay for certain reasons and if given an opportunity, he shall pay the same.

5. The anticipatory bail application is opposed by the learned A.G.A pressing before me the fact that there are direct allegations against the applicant and that the applicant has in fact no defence to offer.
It is stated that the applicant has a criminal history of two cases u/s 376 and 354 I.P.C. which he has not denied.

sentences.text: Prima facie it does not appear that the F.I.R. has been lodged against her for the purpose of bringing disgrace or cause humiliation to her by having her arrested in a mala fide manner.
It may also be kept in mind that anticipatory bail is an extraordinary remedy to be exercised in suitable cases only.
The powers under Section 438 Cr.P.C. cannot be utilized in a routine manner and definitely not as a substitute for regular bail.

This discretionary power calls for existence of facts of the kind where the court is satisfied that its interference is necessary to further the cause of justice and to prevent misuse of process of law.
7. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case I do not find it a fit case for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail.
8. Hence the anticipatory bail application is rejected.

9. It is made clear that observations made in rejecting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on material before him, at any stage of the case.
